questions.q: What does it mean for a character to show "courage" in a story?
questions.a: Courage is the decision to face a situation that is potentially dangerous or unknown. A wrong answer—such as saying "courage means not having any fear"—reveals a misunderstanding that bravery is the absence of fear, rather than acting in spite of it.

questions.q: Why is a "tunnel" often used as a symbol for the unknown in adventure stories?
questions.a: A tunnel is dark and hides what is ahead, representing the uncertainty of the future. If a student says "because tunnels are just for trains," they are missing the symbolic, literary meaning of the setting.

questions.q: If a character enters a mysterious forest because they want to see what is on the other side, are they being courageous? Why?
questions.a: Yes, they are being courageous because they are choosing to leave their comfort zone to explore the unknown. A wrong answer—saying "no, because they might be lost"—fails to distinguish between the risk of adventure and the outcome of the action.

questions.q: Compare a character who stays home to avoid a storm with a character who goes out to watch the lightning. Which one represents the theme of "adventure"?
questions.a: The character watching the storm represents adventure because they are actively engaging with the unknown. A wrong answer suggests the student does not understand that adventure requires participation, not just observation from safety.

questions.q: Is it possible to have an adventure without being courageous? Explain your reasoning.
questions.a: No, because every true adventure involves some level of risk or uncertainty that requires the character to overcome their hesitation. If a student says "yes, you can have an adventure while sitting on a sofa," they are conflating "adventure" with "imagination" rather than the literary theme of taking risks.

questions.q: Write a one-sentence ending for a story where a character stands before a locked, mysterious gate.
questions.a: A good answer will show the character choosing to open the gate despite their fear. A poor answer focuses only on the character being scared and walking away, which fails to capture the theme of adventure.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Courage and adventure are literary themes where a character chooses to face something unknown or ______, rather than avoiding it, to learn more about themselves or the world.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever stood in front of a dark, empty corridor and felt ______ to walk through it?
What is Courage and adventure? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Courage and adventure are literary themes where a character chooses to face something unknown or challenging, rather than avoiding it, to learn more about themselves or the world.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Courage and adventure?
questions.a: Students often believe that "adventure" is only about physical travel to new places (like mountains or space).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify moments of courage in a text and distinguish between actions driven by fear and actions driven by the desire to explore the unknown.
